designs.question: O1: whole-program facts that decide a package's layout or code. (a) [OBJ-1]'s weak count exists only when "some weakref link in the program may name an object" of the class family; (b) [THR-2]'s hand-over compares the weak count of "every object the handed object owns whose class a weakref is made to anywhere in the program"; (c) [WK-18]'s deferred-drop region needs nodes "no other thread can end (not thread_shared, and not reachable from a thread_shared value)". Separate compilation ([BLD-1], [MONO-1], [EFF-4], [BLD-14]) cannot honour any of the three. Design the general rule under which a per-program fact never decides a package's code or layout, and say what each of (a), (b), (c) becomes.
designs.angle: SPEED AND SIMPLICITY FIRST: the shape a careful C programmer would choose, with the fewest bytes, compares and words, as long as the three goals hold.

shape.name: The fact is read from the declaration: a family carries its weak count by `pub` or by its own package's links; a hand-over tests the carrying families through the kind's table; a walk's region is read from `Send`
shape.summary: One principle, `[BLD-16]`: what a package compiles is decided by its own source, the interface files below it and the generic instances it makes, never by a dependant or by the program; a fact of a kind known only while running lives in the kind's table (as `[LT-48]` already does). Applied: (a) a class family carries the 4-byte weak count exactly when, in the package that declares its root base class, some class of the family is `pub`, or a `weakref` type in that package (written, inferred at `weakref x`, or in a generic instance the package makes) names a class of the family; a type that is not a class carries it for its shared values under the same two conditions. The fact is a property of the declaration, recorded with the layout in the interface file, and no dependant can change it: an object of a private class leaves its package only behind `dyn I` or `some I`, so a `weakref` of a value held `dyn I` or `some I` is refused (`E2119` widened), which also closes a silent hole the grammar leaves open (`weakref dyn I` parses, nothing defines it). (b) the hand-over compares the weak count of every owned object whose family carries one, read from its declaration; an object held `dyn I`, or of an `open`/`abstract` class, is walked by the hand-over routine in its kind's table, compiled by the kind's own package beside its `drop` chain (one load, one test, and a call only for a kind with something to test). (c) the region is placed when the node's class is not `Send` (`[THR-8]`): then no owner, no `ref mut` view and no place owning its objects can reach another thread by any route (`[THR-2]`, `[THR-1]`, `[THR-11]`), so no thread but this one ends them. That is stronger than the text's condition (it also covers a scoped task clearing a list through `ref mut`, which today's wording misses), it is read from the class's own words, and a tree walked by a one-thread `parent: weakref Node` is never `Send`, so the walk the rule is written for keeps its region in every package. No new word, no new run-time check, no new run-time data; the `thread_shared` 32-byte header (verdict 101) is untouched.
shape.rule_text:
Part XVII (p17-toolchain.md), after `[BLD-14]`:

* `[BLD-16]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **No fact of the whole program decides a package's code or layout.** The layout of a package's types and the instructions it emits for a line are decided by the package's own source, by the interface files of the packages it depends on, and by the generic instances it makes (`[MONO-1]`); never by a package that depends on it, and never by the program as a whole, which the package never sees (`[BLD-1]`, `[EFF-4]`). A rule that removes an instruction or a header field on a fact of the program states that fact so that the package compiling the line reads it from a declaration it sees (a type's words, its `pub`, whether it is `Send`, `[OBJ-1]`, `[WK-18]`) or, where the fact is one of a kind known only while the program runs, from the kind's own table (`[LT-48]`, `[THR-2]`); where neither holds, the instruction is emitted. Whole-program optimisation (`[DSP-5]`) may remove an instruction with a proof and never changes a layout or what a line does (`[BLD-14]`).

Part VIII (p08-classes.md), `[OBJ-1]`. Replace the sentence "A value a `weakref` link may reach has a third 32-bit number there, its weak count, making 12 bytes: every object of a class family (the classes that share one root base class) of which some `weakref` link in the program may name an object, and every shared value of a type some `weakref` link may name." with:

* `[OBJ-1]` *(changed in 0.9.9)* *(changed in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* … A value of a type that **carries a weak count** has a third 32-bit number there, the weak count, making 12 bytes: every object of a class family (the classes that share one root base class) that carries one, and every `shares` or `shares mut` value of a type that carries one. A class family carries a weak count when, in the package that declares its root base class, a class of the family is `pub`, or a `weakref` type, written, inferred at a `weakref x`, or in a generic instance the package makes, names a class of the family; a type that is not a class carries one under the same two conditions. The fact is read from the declaration and nowhere else, is recorded in the package's interface file with the type's layout (`[BLD-2]`), and no other package can change it (`[BLD-16]`): a `pub` class always carries one, since any dependant may link to it; a private class carries one only when its own package links to it, since its objects leave the package only behind `dyn I` or `some I`, which a `weakref` link never names (`E2119`, `[WK-16]`). A class derived from a `pub open` class in another package carries one, as its base does. … (the rest of the rule unchanged; a `thread_shared` value's header is 32 bytes, verdict 101, and always holds the weak count.)

Part VIII, `[WK-16]`. After "is `E2119`: \"a `weakref` link needs an object that lives on its own; link to the player: `cam.target = weakref player`\"." add:

* `[WK-16]` *(new in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* … A `weakref` of a value held `dyn I` or `some I`, and the type `weakref dyn I`, are `E2119` too: the kind of the object is known only while the program runs, and whether its header holds a weak count is the class's to fix (`[OBJ-1]`): "`weakref dyn Listener` (line 5) names a kind known only while the program runs, and a `weakref` link needs an object whose class fixes its header; link to a base class: write `open class Listener:` with `virtual fn notify(this, msg: StrView): pass` in place of lines 1 and 2, `class Button(Listener):` in place of `class Button implements Listener:` (line 8), and `listeners: Array[weakref Listener] = []` in place of line 5".

Part XI (p11-concurrency.md), `[THR-2]`. Replace "The same is done for every object the handed object owns whose class a `weakref` is made to anywhere in the program (the compiler knows those classes; one compare each), so after `cam.target = weakref level.enemies[0]`, handing `level` over leaves `cam.target` finding enemy 0 ended." with:

* `[THR-2]` *(changed in 0.9.9)* *(changed in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* … The same is done for every object the handed object owns, all the way down, whose class family carries a weak count (`[OBJ-1]`, read from the class's declaration, the same in every package; one compare each), and for no object of a family that carries none, so after `cam.target = weakref level.enemies[0]`, handing `level` over leaves `cam.target` finding enemy 0 ended. The walk follows the handed value's fields and elements by their types; an object held `dyn I`, or of an `open` or `abstract` class (`[CLS-4]`), is walked by the hand-over routine in its kind's table, which its own package compiled beside its `drop` chain, so a kind declared in a package the hand-over's package never saw is walked as any other (`[BLD-16]`); a kind that carries no weak count and owns nothing that does has a null routine there, one load and one test. A value whose type can own no object of a carrying family is handed over with no walk at all. …

Part VIII, `[WK-18]`. Replace "when the node's class has no `drop` method of its own and its objects are ones no other thread can end (not `thread_shared`, and not reachable from a `thread_shared` value), the walk is placed in a **deferred-drop region**" with:

* `[WK-18]` *(new in 0.9.15)* *(changed in 0.9.20)* … when the node's class (the class the link's type names) has no `drop` method of its own and is not `Send` (`[THR-8]`: it holds a `weakref` link to a one-thread target, a `shares` or `shares mut` owner, a `sharedref mut` link or another one-thread part), the walk is placed in a **deferred-drop region**: no owner of such an object, no `ref mut` view of one and no place that owns one reaches another thread by any route (`[THR-2]`, `[THR-1]`, `[THR-11]`), so no thread but this one ends its objects, a fact read from the class's declaration, the same in every package (`[BLD-16]`); a class derived from it is not `Send` either, since it holds the same fields. A tree walked by a `parent: weakref Node` field whose target is a one-thread object is such a class. … Replace "A walk over objects another thread may end pays the count moves." with "A walk over objects of a `Send` class pays the count moves."

Part X (p10-effects.md), the table of `[COST-3]` *(changed in 0.9.20)*. Replace the row "A walk up a tree across a call that may change nodes | guaranteed present | per step, one test of the node's header and one move of the link's weak count (a subtract and an add); where the node's class has no `drop` of its own and no other thread can end its nodes, the walk runs in a deferred-drop region and the count moves go, leaving the header test; …" with "… where the node's class has no `drop` of its own and is not `Send` (`[WK-18]`), the walk runs in a deferred-drop region and the count moves go, leaving the header test; …". Add two rows:

| The weak count in a header | guaranteed present | 4 bytes, and the padding of a first field aligned to 8, in every object of a class family that carries a weak count (`[OBJ-1]`: a family with a `pub` class, or one its own package links to) and in every `shares` value of such a type; none in an object of a private class its package never links to; nothing runs for it |
| An object handed whole to another thread | guaranteed present | one compare of the weak count per object the handed value owns, all the way down, whose family carries one (`[THR-2]`), and a move of its contents to a new block where a link exists; one load and one test, then a call of the kind's routine, per owned object held `dyn I` or of an `open` or `abstract` class; nothing for a value whose type can own no such object |

Part XVII (p17a-codes.md), the row of `E2119`: "a `weakref` of a part (a field, an element stored inline), whose target does not live on its own; a `weakref` of a value held `dyn I` or `some I`, or the type `weakref dyn I`, whose kind is known only while the program runs | `[WK-16]`, `[OBJ-1]`".

Appendix F (p24-appx-f.md), add the row "**carries a weak count** | said of a type whose values have the weak count in their header: a class family with a `pub` class or one its own package links to, and a type that is not a class under the same conditions (`[OBJ-1]`); read from the declaration, never from the program".

Appendix H, H.51: one bullet under "Holes in the memory-safety rules": "No fact of the whole program decides a package's layout or code (`[BLD-16]`): a class family carries its weak count by its `pub` or by its own package's links (`[OBJ-1]`), a hand-over tests the carrying families and walks a hidden kind through its table (`[THR-2]`), a walk's deferred-drop region is read from the class not being `Send` (`[WK-18]`), and a `weakref` never names a `dyn I` or `some I` value (`E2119`, `[WK-16]`); two `[COST-3]` rows."
shape.refuses:
```ember
interface Listener:                       # line 1
    fn notify(this, msg: StrView)         # line 2

class Bus:
    listeners: Array[weakref dyn Listener] = []   # line 5

class Button implements Listener:         # line 8
    fn notify(this, msg: StrView): println(msg)
```
E2119: "`weakref dyn Listener` (line 5) names a kind known only while the program runs, and a `weakref` link needs an object whose class fixes its header; link to a base class: write `open class Listener:` with `virtual fn notify(this, msg: StrView): pass` in place of lines 1 and 2, `class Button(Listener):` in place of `class Button implements Listener:` (line 8), and `listeners: Array[weakref Listener] = []` in place of line 5". The rewritten program compiles: `Listener` is a family root, its `pub`-ness or its package's link gives every `Button` the 12-byte header, and the link is one pointer with one header test to open. (The same code refuses `w = weakref make()` for `fn make() -> some Shape`, with the help naming the class the function returns, `fn make() -> Square`.)
shape.accepts:
A library compiled alone, before any dependant exists:
```ember
# package geom (compiled first, 12-byte headers for Enemy because it is pub)
pub class Enemy:
    hp: int = 10
pub class Level:
    enemies: Array[Enemy] = []
pub fn spawn_wave(ref mut l: Level):
    for _ in 0..3: l.enemies.push(owns Enemy())
```
```ember
# the program, a dependant of geom
import std.thread
from geom import Level, spawn_wave

class Camera:
    target: weakref Enemy = None

fn main():
    level = Level()
    spawn_wave(ref mut level)
    cam = Camera()
    cam.target = weakref level.enemies[0]      # a link into a library object: offset 8 is the weak count there too
    h = thread.spawn(owns fn() owns level: level.enemies.len())
    if cam.target exists as e:
        println(e.hp)
    else:
        println("gone")                        # printed: the hand-over found the link and moved enemy 0
    println(h.join())                          # 3
```
Today's text accepts this on paper and cannot build it: `geom` was compiled without knowing the dependant's `weakref`, so its `push` and its `Enemy()` lay the object out with an 8-byte header and the dependant's `weakref` writes into `hp`. Under the ruling both packages read "`Enemy` is `pub`, so it carries a weak count" from `Enemy`'s declaration, and the hand-over in `main`, compiled by the program, compares the weak count of each `Enemy` the level owns (three compares, `Enemy` is final so no table call). A private, never-linked `class Particle` of the program keeps its 8-byte header, which the always-12-bytes shape would not give it.
shape.cost: What runs: nothing new. Header bytes per object: 4 bytes (8 with the padding of a first field aligned to 8) in every object of a family with a `pub` class or one its own package links to, which is today's 12-byte case widened from "linked anywhere" to "linkable from anywhere"; 8-byte headers stay for every private class the package never links to, which is where a program's numerous objects (its own particles, cells, nodes) live. Compares per hand-over: one per owned object of a carrying family, all the way down, as today for linked classes (verdict 114: 10,000 enemies, 10,000 compares), plus one load and one test per owned object held `dyn I` or of an `open`/`abstract` class, and the routine's call only when that kind has something to test; zero for a value whose static type can own no carrying object (an `Array[int]`, a struct of numbers, a tree of private unlinked classes). What a walk pays: unchanged per step; the region is kept for every tree walked by a one-thread `parent: weakref Node` field (the class is not `Send`) and dropped only for a `Send` node class, whose count moves are two plain adds per step. Section X.4 rows: the walk row's condition becomes "has no `drop` of its own and is not `Send`"; two rows added, "The weak count in a header | guaranteed present | 4 bytes, and the padding of a first field aligned to 8, in every object of a class family that carries a weak count (`[OBJ-1]`) and every `shares` value of such a type; none in an object of a private class its package never links to; nothing runs for it" and "An object handed whole to another thread | guaranteed present | one compare of the weak count per owned object of a carrying family, all the way down, and a move to a new block where a link exists; one load and one test, then the kind's routine, per owned object held `dyn I` or of an `open` or `abstract` class; nothing for a value whose type can own no such object" (today the hand-over compare has no row, which `[COST-5]` forbids).
shape.build: Package compile: for every class family whose root base class the package declares, carries = (some class of the family is `pub`) or (a `weakref T` type, written, inferred at a `weakref x`, or in a generic instance this package makes, names a class of the family); the same per non-class type for its `shares` blocks. The front end knows this before layout, from the package's own source and the instances `[MONO-1]` assigns it; it fixes the header size (8 or 12) and every field offset, and writes the fact into the interface file beside the layout, so it is in the interface hash (`[BLD-2]`) and a dependant deriving `class Boss(Enemy)` lays `Boss` out on a 12-byte header. For a `weakref` of a `dyn I` or `some I` value the type checker refuses (`E2119`). For every class the package emits, beside the `drop` chain in the kind's table, a hand-over routine: for each owned field and element of a carrying family, one compare of the weak count and, where a link exists, the move to a new block and the ended mark on the old; for each owned field held `dyn I` or of an `open`/`abstract` class, a load of that kind's routine and a call when it is not null; the entry is null when the kind carries nothing and owns nothing that does. The hand-over site (`thread.spawn`, a channel send, `jobs.submit`, a callback C keeps) calls the handed value's routine directly for a final class, and the walk for a struct or collection is emitted inline by its type. For (c) the walk's package tests `Send` of the class the link's type names, computed from the class's fields in the interface file exactly as `[THR-8]` computes it for a bound, and emits the region's enter and leave (one add and one subtract of the thread's counter) or the count moves. Link time: nothing; the kind tables are ordinary data, deduplicated as `[MONO-1]` says. Run time: nothing beyond the rows above.
shape.owner_verdicts: Verdict 101 (the `thread_shared` 32-byte header, home/away counts, the queue): untouched; the thread_shared header keeps its weak count at offset 8 and its layout, and nothing in (a), (b) or (c) reads or changes it. Verdict 114, fix 1 ("every object the handed object owns whose class a weakref is made to anywhere in the program (the compiler knows those classes)"): touched, not reversed. The compared set changes from "classes linked anywhere in the program" to "families that carry a weak count", which contains every linked class, since a class a link names is `pub` or linked in its own package; the behaviour the verdict asked for (`cam.target` says "gone", nothing refused, nothing stops, one compare per object) is kept, and the only change is that a hand-over of a tree of `pub` objects pays its compares even in a program that makes no link, which the verdict's own 10,000-compare example already accepts as the price. Verdict 103 (a whole value is shared) and the rest: untouched.

designs.against_the_other_angle: The opposite angle (generality and safety first, a rule with no conditions) would take one of two shapes. (1) Every object and every shared value carries the weak count, 12-byte headers everywhere; a `weakref dyn I` is then legal, since every kind has the slot. Against it: it pays 4 bytes, and 8 after the padding of a first `int`, `f64`, `String` or pointer field (Ember's `int` is `i64`, so almost every object pays 8), on every object of every private class a program never links to, which are exactly the numerous ones (particles, grid cells, ECS components held as objects); a million such objects is 8 MB and a size class up (24-byte payload: 32 bytes a block today, 40 rounded to 48 tomorrow), and `[COST-1]` is lost for the plainest program, since C upholding the same invariant carries no weak count in a struct nothing weakly points at. It buys only `weakref dyn I`, which the text never writes, which the grammar admits by silence, and which the class-family shape gives with one pointer and one header test (`weakref Listener` over an `open class Listener`): the observer pattern is not lost, it is written with the word the document already has for \"objects of several kinds behind one name with identity\", a base class. (2) The lead's leaning taken literally, \"a private class is reachable from nowhere else\": it is reachable, behind `dyn I` and `some I`, and a dependant's `weakref` of such a value would write into the first field of an 8-byte-header object; a rule that keeps 8-byte headers must say what a `weakref` may name, or it is memory corruption by silence, so the refusal of `weakref dyn I` is not an extra, it is what makes the conditional header sound. The same angle would add a word (`@linkable`, `interface Listener: needs Linked`) to keep 8-byte headers on `pub` classes too; against it: a word is the owner's (O2 waits for one already), it puts a Rust-style annotation on every library class an application might ever link to, and it fails the Python-readability goal for a saving the measurement cannot see (a library's objects are a program's few, not its many). For (c), the other angle would drop the region from every `pub` class's walk, or keep today's whole-program condition and have the root package re-link the library; against both: the `Send` test is read from the class's own fields in every package, costs nothing, keeps the region for the one tree shape `[WK-18]` is written for (a one-thread `parent: weakref Node` makes the class not `Send`), and is the only condition that is actually sufficient, since today's \"not thread_shared and not reachable from one\" lets a scoped task holding `ref mut` to the owning list end a node on another thread while the walking thread defers its block.
designs.open_risks: 1. O2 is load-bearing for (c): \"not `Send`\" reads `weakref Node` as a link to a one-thread target; if the owner rules that `weakref T`'s type does not say whether its target is `thread_shared`, the walk over a class whose only one-thread part is that link cannot be judged from the class, and the region falls back to \"the class holds a `shares`, `shares mut` or `sharedref mut` part\" (rarer) or is dropped. 2. `[WK-18]`'s other condition, \"no `drop` method of its own\", is read here as the named class's own `drop` (visible); if its reason extends to a derived class's `drop` in another package, that condition is a per-program fact too and needs the same treatment (the derived class's `drop` is in its kind's table, so the region could test the table's entry once per walked kind, one load and one test). 3. The hand-over routine for `open`/`abstract` classes and `dyn I` fields adds a virtual call per such owned object (as the `drop` chain already has); the null-routine test keeps it to one load and one test for kinds with nothing to compare, but a tree of 10,000 `open`-class objects each owning a linked child pays 10,000 calls at a hand-over, not 10,000 compares; the compiler may devirtualise with `[DSP-5]` when the whole program is visible. 4. `shares` values of `pub` types (every `shares Array[int]`, since `Array` is `pub` in `std`) now always carry the weak count, 4 bytes each; a finer rule for shared values of generic types (carry by the outermost declared type) was chosen for simplicity and over-approximates. 5. `E2119`'s widening and `[BLD-16]` are new text a compiler must implement: today's `codes.rs` test holds (no new code), but `rule_index.py`'s cost-row check wants the two rows. 6. The 12-byte header's padding before an 8-aligned first field (effectively 16 bytes) is a layout cost `[OBJ-1]`'s table has always had; placing one 4-byte field at offset 12 would recover it, but field order is declaration order in `[OBJ-1]` and reordering is the owner's. 7. Verdict 114 fix 1 is touched (the compared set widens from \"linked anywhere\" to \"carrying families\"); the owner should confirm that a link-free program paying the compares on a hand-over of `pub` objects is within what the verdict accepted.

shape.name: Declared layout: the weak count, the hand-over walk and the walk's region follow the type's own declaration, never the program
shape.summary: One new rule, [BLD-16]: what a package compiles (its types' layouts, its functions' code, the tests a line keeps or drops) is decided by the package's own text and the interface files it imports, never by which lines elsewhere write a word on its values; a rule whose condition is such a fact reads it from the type's declaration, from the value's type at the line, or from the kind's own table while running ([LT-48]'s shape), and takes the safe side where the declaration leaves it open. Then: (a) [OBJ-1]: a type's values carry the weak count when the type can be named from outside its package (a class of its family, or the type, is `pub`, is named in a `pub` item's signature, or an object of it is put behind an interface type anywhere in the package) or when a `weakref` in its own package names it; decided by the declaring package, recorded in the interface file as part of the layout and as a TypeInfo flag. The lead's 'a private class is reachable from nowhere else' is incomplete: a private class escapes through `pub fn make() -> some Shape`, through a `pub` list of `owns dyn Shape`, and through an inferred type from a `pub` signature; the three exits above close that. (b) [THR-2]: the compare runs over every owned object whose type carries the weak count, through a per-type hand-over function kept in TypeInfo beside the drop functions and generated by the declaring (for a generic instance, the instantiating) package, which calls the functions of the types its fields own; a type whose table says it owns nothing with a weak count is handed over with no walk. (c) [WK-18]: the region is given when the node's class has no `drop` of its own and no other thread can end the walked objects, read from types: now, when the class is not `Send` (its objects can be neither `thread_shared` nor owned by a `thread_shared` value, [THR-8]/[THR-1]); once O2's word says a link's kind, when the walk's link is of the one-thread kind. For that to be sound, [THR-2] gains the sentence Rust gets from `Rc`-in-`Arc` being impossible: a one-thread `weakref` link is made only to an object reached through this thread's own owners, so `weakref scene.players[0]` with `scene: thread_shared Scene` is `E7015`, and a call giving such a view to a function whose summary says it makes a one-thread link to that parameter (`this` included; [BLD-14] item 8) is `E7015` at the call. [DSP-5], [WK-17], [CLS-12] stay: they remove tests or are conditioned on the interface already; the final link may only remove what every program would let it remove.
shape.rule_text:
**p17-toolchain.md, §XVII.3, after `[BLD-14]`:**

* `[BLD-16]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **A per-program fact never decides a package's code or layout.** What a package compiles (the layout of its types, the code of its functions, the tests a line keeps or drops) is decided by the package's own text and by what the interface files of the packages it imports record (`[MOD-9]`, `[EFF-4]`, `[BLD-14]`), never by a fact of the program that will use it: which lines, anywhere, write a word on a value of one of its types, which of its values are made `thread_shared`, which of its classes a `weakref` names. A rule whose condition would be such a fact reads it from the type's own declaration (the weak count in a header, `[OBJ-1]`; the hand-over of an object another thread takes, `[THR-2]`; a walk's deferred-drop region, `[WK-18]`), from the value's type at the line (the kind of a link), or from the kind's own table while the program runs (`[LT-48]`), and where the declaration leaves it open takes the side that is safe in every program. With the whole program visible, the final link may remove only what every program would let it remove (a virtual call with one reachable implementation, `[DSP-5]`): it changes no layout and no meaning. So a package compiled once lays out its objects, and tests what it tests, the same in every program that uses it, in `ember check` of the package alone, in its tests, and in a module loaded at run time (`[ABI-1]`, `[VER-4]`).

```ember

pub class Mesh:
    verts: Array[f32] = []

# package app, built later against geom's interface file
from geom import Mesh
class Camera:
    target: weakref Mesh = None
```

Prints `0`. Under today's `[OBJ-1]` no `weakref` in `geom` names a `Mesh`, so `geom`'s compiled code lays `verts` at offset 8, while `app`'s `weakref m` adds to a weak count at offset 8: the same bytes, a corrupted list, unless the whole of `geom` is compiled again for `app`. Under this ruling `Mesh` is `pub`, so `geom` itself gives every `Mesh` the 12-byte header, records it in its interface file, and `app` compiles its link against that layout. Likewise a library's walk (`[WK-18]`) over its own non-`Send` `Node` class gets its deferred-drop region whatever a program does, and a library function's hand-over of a `Level` compares the weak count of each `Enemy` it owns through `Level`'s hand-over function, whether or not the program that calls it ever writes `weakref level.enemies[0]`. The per-program shape accepts none of these as a package compiled once; the lead's leaning accepts the first but lays out an 8-byte header for a private class returned as `some Shape` from a `pub fn`, which a dependant then links to.
shape.cost: What runs: nothing new per line. Header bytes: 4 (8 where the first field is 8-aligned) on every value of a type that can be named from outside its package or that a `weakref` in its package names; 0 on a private, unexposed, unlinked type; a `thread_shared` value's 32-byte header is unchanged (verdict 101). Against the per-program shape: a `pub` class that no program links to pays 4 to 8 bytes it did not; against Rust's `Rc` (always both counts, 16 bytes) and the lead's shape, the same or less. Compares per hand-over: one per handed object and per owned object whose type carries the weak count, through the type's hand-over function; none for a type whose table says it carries none and owns none (the compiler reads the flag from the interface file and emits no call); 10,000 enemies owned by a handed `Level` are 10,000 compares, as in verdict 114, now also when no program links to an `Enemy`. A walk: unchanged where the region is given (one header test per step, one add and one subtract of a per-thread counter per region); a walk over a `Send` class's nodes through the walker's own link pays the count moves (a subtract and an add per step) until O2's word lets the link's type give the region; a walk through links to `thread_shared` nodes pays them always, as today. The `[COST-3]` rows: new "The weak count in a header | guaranteed present | 4 bytes in the header of every value of a type that can be named from outside its package or that a `weakref` in its package names, 8 where the first field is 8-aligned; none for a type private to its package that no `weakref` in it names; a `thread_shared` value's 32-byte header carries it always"; new "An object handed to another thread | guaranteed present | one compare of the weak count for the handed object and for each object it owns whose type carries one, through the type's hand-over function; nothing for a type that carries none and owns none; a copy into a new block only for an object a link names" (today's table has no row for verdict 114's compares, which `[COST-5]` requires); and the walk row's condition reworded as in rule_text.
shape.build: Package compile (the declaring package): for each type it declares, the front end computes 'can be named from outside' from the package's own text: the type or a class of its family is `pub`; it appears in a `pub` item's signature (a syntactic walk of `pub` declarations, generic arguments included); an upcast of one of its objects or shared values to `dyn I` or `some I` occurs anywhere in the package (every such coercion is a resolution step the compiler already performs, §IV.11); or a `weakref` expression in the package has a value of the type as its operand. The result, per class family (root base class) and per struct or enum type, fixes the header (8 or 12) and every field offset; it is written into the interface file as part of the type's layout (`[BLD-2]` already hashes layouts) and into the type's `TypeInfo` flags. For each type the package also generates the hand-over function (as it generates drop functions): for each field that owns an object or shared value whose type carries the weak count, one compare, a copy into a new block and the ended mark when a link exists, and a call of the owned type's hand-over function for fields whose type's flag 'owns values with a weak count' is set; through the object's own table for a `dyn I` field; a generic type's function is generated by the instantiating package, like its drop ([MONO-1] dedups it at link). A second flag, 'owns nothing with a weak count', is computed from the field types' flags and recorded. For each function the summary gains item 8: which view parameters, `this` included, the body makes a one-thread `weakref` link to (transitively through callees' summaries, as items 1 and 5 are). Link: the type's `TypeInfo` and the layout hash per type are checked across packages as any interface hash; a module loaded at run time carries the same layouts because they depend on nothing outside its own sources (`[ABI-1]`, `[VER-4]`). Compile of a using package: at `weakref x` it reads the operand type's flag from the interface file; a type with the flag clear can only have reached it by an unlisted route and is `E0901`. At a hand-over line it reads the handed type's two flags: emits nothing for a type that carries none and owns none, else the compare and the call of the type's hand-over function. At a `weakref x` line of the one-thread kind it checks the place analysis of `x` (`[BRW-17]`) for a `thread_shared` value on the path, and at every call it checks each argument reached through a `thread_shared` value against the callee's item-8 summary; both `E7015`. At a walk with a link it reads the node class's 'has own drop' and `Send` facts from the interface file (and, once O2 lands, the link's kind from its type) and places the region or the count moves. Run time: the hand-over function and the flags live in `TypeInfo`; nothing else changes. Nothing the whole program knows reaches any package's code generation; the final link's `[DSP-5]` devirtualisation stays, since it removes an indirect call every program would let it remove and touches no layout.
shape.owner_verdicts: 114 (touched, not reversed): its fix 1 reads "every object the handed object owns whose class a `weakref` is made to anywhere in the program (the compiler knows those classes)"; this ruling keeps the one-compare-per-owned-object price and the move-and-mark mechanism, and widens the compared set to 'every owned object whose type carries the weak count', which a package can know on its own; the parenthesis 'the compiler knows those classes' is what separate compilation cannot honour. 101 (not touched): the 32-byte `thread_shared` header already carries the weak count in every program; this ruling gives one-thread objects the same program-independence and changes no byte of that header. 59 (its spirit touched, not its ruling): the owner chose 32-bit counts over 64-bit to spare 4 to 8 bytes per shared object; this ruling keeps 32-bit counts and adds 4 (or 8 by alignment) bytes only to objects of types a dependant can name, which today pay it as soon as any program links to them.

designs.against_the_other_angle: The opposite angle (as fast as C first) keeps the program-wide decision and makes the build honour it: every package is compiled from source for each program, the set of classes a `weakref` names, the classes a `thread_shared` value can reach and the hand-over compares are worked out over the whole program before any package's code generation, and the cache of `[BLD-2]` is keyed on that set, so a `pub` class no program links to keeps its 8-byte header and the hand-over of a `Level` nobody links into costs nothing. The case against it. (1) It is not separate compilation, only a build that recompiles dependencies: adding the first `weakref` to a library class recompiles the library and every package between, which `[BLD-1]` and `[BLD-2]` promise not to do, and `ember check` of a library alone, its own tests (`[TST-*]`), and an IDE lay the class out differently from the program that uses it, so a diagnostic or a benchmark of the library is of another program. (2) It cannot hold at all where compilation is separate by construction: a module loaded at run time (`[FFI-28]`, `[ABI-2]`) and a hot-reload image (Annex B) are compiled without the host; the same class then has two header layouts in one process, and `[VER-4]`'s 'the object header is stable within a major version' becomes false, since a header that changes with a use is not an ABI. No link-time check can catch it for a run-time load except a per-type layout hash, which would refuse to load a plugin because the host wrote `weakref` somewhere: a refusal of a correct program. (3) The owner's own hardening already settled the pattern: `[LT-48]` compared kinds the program knew and let a kind from an unseen package through; the fix put the fact into the kind's table, and H.51 records why. (a), (b) and (c) are the same shape with worse consequences (a layout, not a check). (4) The saving is 4 to 8 bytes per object of an exported family that no program links to, and nothing on private families, which both shapes lay out at 8 bytes; a hand-over's compares are paid only by programs that hand over objects owning such families, one load and compare each, far below the move itself. Against that, the Rust-style guarantee that a type's layout is a function of its declaration is what makes a compiled library a library. (5) For (c) the whole-program shape needs 'no `thread_shared` value anywhere reaches a `Node`', which a dependant can falsify after the library's walk was compiled with its region; the only layout-free way to keep that region is the one above: a type fact (`Send`) or a link kind in the type, which the per-program shape would also need as soon as modules load at run time. The lead's leaning is on the right side but incomplete: 'a private class is reachable from nowhere else' is false for a private class returned as `some I`, held behind a `pub` `Array[owns dyn I]`, or named in a `pub` signature and taken by inference; the three exit conditions close it at no cost to the private case.
designs.open_risks: (1) (c)'s full form and the refused program's fix lines depend on O2 (the owner's word for a link to a `thread_shared` target, proposed `weakref thread_shared T`); until it lands, the region is given only to a non-`Send` node class, and a walk over a `Send` class through the walker's own link pays the count moves; the `E7015` message's fix lines must follow whatever spelling O2 chooses. (2) Whether `weakref dyn I` or a `weakref` of a `some I` value is a type is unspecified today (`[WK-11]` says the target is a class object or a shared value; the grammar parses `weakref base_type`); the interface-type exit in `[OBJ-1]` is conservative (it only adds the count) and can be dropped if the owner rules such links out. (3) `@reflect` field descriptors may be a route by which a dependant reaches a private class's objects; the `E0901` clause refuses a `weakref` on such a value rather than guessing, and a second pass should say whether reflection names private types. (4) `[FFI-35a]` says an object given to C under `retained` is 'marked in its header as kept by C', while `[OBJ-1]` says an object carries 'no flags but a `thread_shared` value's three marks', and a one-thread weak count checked at 4,294,967,295 has no free bit: where that mark lives must be said (a separate rule; not per-program, so outside O1). (5) The root package's `pub` classes, and shared values of `std`'s `pub` struct types (`shares String`), now always carry the weak count, 4 to 8 bytes each; the owner may prefer a narrower exit set (for instance only a class named in a `pub` signature, not merely declared `pub`), which keeps the ruling's shape. (6) Item 8 of `[BLD-14]` makes a method that writes `child.parent = weakref this` uncallable on an object inside a `thread_shared` value; that is the intended Rust-equivalent outcome (such a tree is a `thread_shared` tree with `weakref thread_shared` links), but it changes the accepted set, so `[VER-9]` applies. (7) The deferred-drop region must also hold back the old block a hand-over inside the walk leaves behind (its last link may hold no count in the region); the existing text's 'only their blocks' memory waits' covers it if read as every block of the node's family freed inside the region, which the region's implementation note should say outright.

judgement.question: O1: whole-program facts that decide a package's layout or code. (a) [OBJ-1]'s weak count exists only when some weakref link in the program may name an object of the class family; (b) [THR-2]'s hand-over compares the weak count of every owned object whose class a weakref is made to anywhere in the program; (c) [WK-18]'s deferred-drop region needs nodes no other thread can end (not thread_shared, not reachable from a thread_shared value). Separate compilation ([BLD-1], [MONO-1], [EFF-4], [BLD-14]) cannot honour any of the three. Design the general rule under which a per-program fact never decides a package's code or layout, and say what each of (a), (b), (c) becomes; price each shape; say whether verdict 101 is touched.

scores.notes: Sound for every route it lists, and its (c) is the only condition that is actually sufficient (a non-`Send` object reaches no task, no job and no thread). Two holes left open: a private class named in a `pub` signature (a `pub fn make() -> Square`, a `pub` field of type `Inner`, a `pub` alias) gives a dependant a value of a private type by inference, and nothing in Part V forbids it, so the dependant's `weakref` writes into an 8-byte header; and a derived class's `drop` in another package falsifies `[WK-18]`'s 'no `drop` of its own' (the shape names it as risk 2 and does not fix it). A function value's state inside a handed object is not walked (its layout is its maker's, as a `dyn I`'s is). Otherwise buildable from the text, minimal bytes, no new word, no new run-time data; the `E2119` widening is what makes an 8-byte header sound at all.

scores.shape: Shape 2 (safety and separate compilation first): declared layout with three exits, a hand-over function in TypeInfo, region from `Send` or from the link's kind, `E7015` for a one-thread link through a `thread_shared` value
scores.notes: Its `pub`-signature exit closes a real hole shape 1 misses, and its `E7015` sentence (a one-thread `weakref` link names only an object reached through this thread's own owners) is a real hole in `[THR-2]` as written ('any function that may run on another thread than its target's owner' names no thread when the owner is a `thread_shared` value). But its second disjunct for (c), 'the walk's link is of the one-thread kind', is unsound: a scoped task given `ref mut` to the list that owns `Send` nodes ends one on its own thread, whose per-thread deferred-drop counter is zero, and frees the block the walker's count-free link still names; `[THR-11]` sees no conflict because the parent is blocked in the join. Its interface-type exit pays 4 to 8 bytes on every private class ever coerced to `dyn I` for a type (`weakref dyn I`) it leaves undefined, so the bytes buy nothing. Its rule text and its cost row disagree on a `Send` class's walk ('until O2 lands'). Long, with a `TypeInfo` flag and a per-type function for every type, where shape 1 needs the routine only for kinds whose layout the handing package cannot see. Function-value state not walked either.

scores.shape: The lead's leaning: weak count on every object of a `pub` class or of a class its own package links to; (b) over those classes; (c) only for a class whose objects can never be `thread_shared`, read from its type

**Part XVII (p17-toolchain.md), §XVII.3, after `[BLD-14]`, new rule:**

* `[BLD-16]` *(new in 0.9.20)* **No fact of the whole program decides a package's code or layout.** The layout of a package's types and the instructions it emits for a line are decided by the package's own source, by the interface files of the packages it imports (`[MOD-9]`, `[EFF-4]`, `[BLD-14]`) and by the generic instances it makes (`[MONO-1]`); never by a package that depends on it, and never by the program as a whole, which the package never sees (`[BLD-1]`): not by which lines, anywhere, write a word on a value of one of its types, not by which of its values are made `thread_shared`, not by which of its classes a `weakref` names. A rule whose condition would be such a fact states it so that the package compiling the line reads it from a declaration it sees (a type's words, its `pub`, whether it is `Send`: `[OBJ-1]`, `[WK-18]`), from the type of the place at the line (`[THR-2]`), or, where the fact is one of a kind known only while the program runs, from the kind's own table (`[LT-48]`, `[THR-2]`); where none of these holds, the instruction is emitted and the test is paid. With the whole program visible, the final link may remove only what every program would let it remove (a virtual call with one reachable implementation, `[DSP-5]`): it changes no layout and no meaning (`[BLD-14]`). So a package compiled once lays out its objects, and tests what it tests, the same in every program that uses it, in `ember check` of the package alone, in its tests, in a hot-reload image and in a module loaded at run time (`[ABI-1]`, `[VER-4]`).

judgement.final_cost: What runs: nothing new per line, no new run-time data beyond a flag and a routine pointer in each `TypeInfo`. Header bytes per object: 4 (8 where the first field is 8-aligned: almost every object, since `int` is `i64`) on every object of a class family that is `pub`, named in a `pub` signature, or linked in its own package, and on every `shares` value of such a type (`shares int`, `shares Array[T]` included, `int` and `Array` being `std`'s `pub` types); 0 on a private or `pub(package)` type its package never links to, where a program's numerous objects live; the `thread_shared` 32-byte header unchanged (verdict 101). Against today's text: the 12-byte case widens from 'linked anywhere' to 'linkable from anywhere'; against Rust's `Rc` (always both counts): the same or less. Compares per hand-over: one per handed object and per owned object, all the way down, whose family carries one (10,000 enemies, 10,000 compares, verdict 114, now also when no program links to an `Enemy`); one load and one test, then a call, per owned value of hidden layout (`dyn I`, `open`/`abstract` class, a function value's state), the call only for a kind with something to compare; zero for a value whose static type can own no carrying object (an `Array[int]`, a struct of numbers, a tree of private unlinked classes). What a walk pays: unchanged per step (one header test) where the region is given, now for every tree whose node class is not `Send` (a one-thread `parent: weakref Node` makes it so) and has no `drop` another package could add; a walk over a `Send` class, or over a `pub open` class, pays the count moves (a subtract and an add per step) as a walk over `thread_shared` nodes always did. Two new `[COST-3]` rows (the hand-over compare had none, which `[COST-5]` forbids) and the walk row's condition reworded. Compile time: the three exits are a syntactic walk of the package's `pub` declarations plus the `weakref` types it writes or infers; the hand-over routine is generated beside each `drop`; item 8 is one more bit per parameter in the summary; nothing at link time.
